solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fights to eat animal product? They don't.

indicators.note: to eat means one word swallows the other, so the fighting word goes round the product

parts.note: fights here is a verb: vies, competes
an egg is a product taken from an animal

explanation.surface: A question about combatants who devour animal products, answered with a wry 'They don't'.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the closing remark: the people who don't eat animal products. Strictly that is vegans, but the colloquial term stretches to cover them.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetarians, informally named, are the people who refuse to eat animal produce, so 'They don't' points at them.

clue.text: Cleric might be the answer to this negative feedback

parts.words: Cleric might be the answer to this
parts.note: read as wordplay, 'vicious' is an anagram signal acting on the letters of circle, and they rearranged give cleric

explanation.surface: A churchman offered as the reply to some unwelcome criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer works as a clue whose solution is the word Cleric, 'vicious' being the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle in which a bad effect feeds back to worsen its own cause is a self-reinforcing loop of harm.

clue.text: Ground for breaking up? She'd nag

indicators.note: breaking up suggests the words fall apart and are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A reason to end a relationship: she would keep nagging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a noun, a reason; it is the past tense of grind, as of teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth that are ground together in anger or pain are said to be gnashed.

clue.text: Religious meal provided by sailor

parts.note: provided means on condition that, if
a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A faith-based dinner laid on by a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Muslims break the Ramadan daytime fast with this evening meal at sunset.

clue.text: How to make strap for protection around hole

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer's words say the letter S joined with a trap, and together they spell strap

explanation.surface: Instructions for making a protective band to fit round an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer's words read as a recipe that builds strap. The definition is a golf bunker guarding the green.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course a sandy bunker guards the green and its cup from stray approach shots.

clue.text: Wood trim

definitions.meaning: the timber of a type of conifer
as an adjective, neat and smart in appearance

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a conifer and its timber; the other is an adjective for neat and well turned out.

clue.text: Not standing down in advance is dignified

indicators.note: in advance means the letter is brought forward to an earlier place

parts.note: someone not standing is seated
D is the abbreviation for down, as in crossword clue numbers

explanation.surface: Sitting down early is thought to be a mark of good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving D two places earlier in SEATED gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm, composed and unhurried, which is what a dignified manner is.

clue.text: Peculiar revolutionary repeatedly claimed right to follow religious education

indicators.note: to follow means the revolutionary part comes after the religious education

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education

indicators.note: claimed means taken in, so the doubled name holds the right letter
repeatedly means the name appears twice over

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: An odd rebel kept asserting a right to study religion after school RE.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles CHE to CHECHE, and 'claimed' puts R inside it, between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Recherché means rare, exotic or obscure, chosen for its unusualness, close to strange or odd.

clue.text: Authorise fraud on company

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a fraud is a con
a company is a firm

explanation.surface: Signing off a swindle committed against a business.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm a decision or appointment is to ratify or sanction it formally.

clue.text: Edward chased virgin and was scolded

indicators.note: chased means one word comes running after the other, so the Edward word follows

parts.note: a virgin is chaste
Ned is a familiar form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward pursued a maiden and got a telling-off for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chased' reads as part of the pursuit story but only says the Edward name comes after the virgin word; 'and was' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be chastened is to be rebuked or humbled, a close synonym for being told off.

clue.text: Some change medical specialism to disrupt poison gas

indicators.note: to disrupt means the specialism breaks into the middle of the gas

parts.note: CS gas is a tear gas used in riot control
ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine

explanation.surface: A call to switch a hospital department so it can stop a gas attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins of small value, US and other pennies, are a kind of loose coinage carried in the pocket.

clue.text: Successful model might be doing this

definitions.meaning: an idiom for being comfortably well placed
an artist's model poses seated and looking attractive

explanation.surface: A top fashion model and what such a person might be up to.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a fortunate position, and literally pictures someone posing seated and attractive.

clue.text: Describing article alternatively comprehended?

indicators.note: comprehended is used in its old sense of enclosed, so one word holds the article within it

parts.note: alternatively can be expressed by the conjunction or
the definite article is 'the'

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether some written item was understood in a different way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue gives the wordplay, and as a whole it hints at the answer: a word used of something seen alternatively, a different one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something alternative or different, the one besides, as in 'the article on the other side'.

clue.text: Where blade should be fixed completely

definitions.meaning: a blade is driven in right up to the handle
an idiom meaning fully, to the utmost

explanation.definitionFit: The hilt is a sword's handle, so a blade plunged that far is in all the way; hence the idiom for totally.

clue.text: Team not made up of stars

parts.note: a team is a side
something not made up is real

explanation.surface: A squad of genuine players rather than an invented lineup of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' tempts toward celebrities in a team; it is the astronomical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal is the astronomical adjective for things relating to or measured by the fixed stars.

clue.text: Richard Sheridan started accepting playwright gigs

indicators.note: accepting means the first part takes in the playwright

parts.note: Rick is a short form of Richard

indicators.note: started means only the first letter of the surname is taken

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw is the playwright

explanation.surface: Richard Brinsley Sheridan, himself a playwright, taking on writing commissions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gigs' looks like engagements; it is the old word for light two-wheeled carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a light two-wheeled carriage; rickshaws are two-wheeled passenger carts pulled by a runner.

clue.text: Hoax animal mostly is seafood

parts.note: a hoax is a scam

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the animal is used

parts.note: the pig is the animal

explanation.surface: A fake creature turns out to be nothing but a plate of seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustines, usually breaded and fried, a staple seafood dish in Britain.

clue.text: Complaints result from horrible mail sent

indicators.note: something horrible is a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Grievances follow when nasty letters are posted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaints' looks like grievances; it is the medical sense, illnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or disorder, like a minor illness.

clue.text: Knock politician for blocking one piece of legislation

indicators.note: blocking means the politician gets in the way between the other parts

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a law passed by parliament is an act
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Criticising a politician for obstructing a single bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock' looks like a verb meaning criticise; here it is the noun, a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is a forceful collision or blow, as is a knock.

clue.text: Help to paint female friend?

parts.note: a pal is a friend
-ette is a suffix marking a female form, as in usherette

explanation.surface: A girlfriend asked to lend a hand with some decorating.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: a female pal would be a 'pal-ette'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist mixes colours on this board, so it is an aid to painting.

clue.text: Could some reflection of Gogol be vilified by contemporary journalism?

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the letters read right to left
some means only part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a Russian writer might be trashed by modern online reporting.
explanation.definitionFit: A live blog is a running online report updated as events happen, a modern journalistic form.

clue.text: Forgiving destruction of headless sentinel

indicators.note: destruction of means the word is smashed and its letters rebuilt
headless means the first letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: Showing mercy by sparing a guard who has been beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' drops the S to leave ENTINEL, and 'destruction of' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means tolerant and merciful, inclined to excuse faults rather than punish.

clue.text: Desire soft touch

parts.note: p is piano, the musical marking for soft
to touch on a topic is to refer to it

explanation.surface: Wanting a gentle caress.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefer one thing is to want it more, to favour or wish for it.

clue.text: Milk for baby colt might initially sour if curdled

indicators.note: curdled milk has gone lumpy and changed form, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word colt, the initial letter of might, and the word sour make up the pool of letters

explanation.surface: A warning that a foal's milk could turn sour if it curdles.
explanation.definitionFit: Colostrum is the first milk a mother mammal produces after giving birth, fed to the newborn.

clue.text: Angel Metatron's closing portal on both sides

indicators.note: the portal sits on both sides of the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a portal is a door

indicators.note: closing means the final letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: The archangel Metatron shutting a gateway from either side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angel' looks like a heavenly being, alongside Metatron; it is the theatrical sense, a financial backer.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a backer who gives money to a venture, such as a show, so a giver or benefactor.

clue.text: Play with first labelled whisky sample?

indicators.note: labelled means the sample carries a tag, which follows it

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky
A is the first letter, or a first-class grade

explanation.surface: Tasting whisky with the first sample tagged for identification.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a piece of theatre, and drama is the general term for such works.

clue.text: Run over

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a run not scored off the bat (a bye or wide) is called this
as an adjective, more than needed, surplus

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a run given away by the bowling side through wides, byes or no-balls goes down as one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket run not credited to a batter has this name, and anything left over is surplus to need.

clue.text: Good-time girl not short of love for Fanny

parts.note: a good time is fun
dame is slang for a woman or girl

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the love letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written before losing a letter
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A party girl who has love to spare for a woman named Fanny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fanny' looks like a girl's name; it is slang for the backside, the American sense (in Britain it is ruder).
explanation.definitionFit: Fundament is a formal or jocular word for the buttocks, and fanny is US slang for the same part.

clue.text: Decimals or some other mathematical concept

parts.note: the decimal system counts in tens
taken as written

explanation.surface: Listing decimals among a range of mathematical ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some other' sets this concept beside decimals, the earlier mathematical idea in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tensor is a mathematical object generalising vectors and matrices, used in physics and geometry.

clue.text: Skin disfigurement concealed in pitch black

indicators.note: concealed in means the blemish is hidden inside the other word

parts.note: to pitch is to throw, and shy means a throw
a wart is a growth on the skin

explanation.surface: A blemish on the skin goes unseen in total darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch black' reads as one phrase, but 'pitch' is the throw and 'black' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarthy describes a dark complexion, so dusky or dark-skinned, loosely black.
